definitions.explanation: To break something by bending or applying pressure. The transitive form—someone breaks something.
To fold paper or other flexible materials. Used for origami and folding.

examples.japanese: {紙|かみ}を{折|お}って{鶴|つる}を{作|つく}る。
examples.english: Fold paper to make a crane.

examples.japanese: {足|あし}を{折|お}ってしまった。

notes:
TRANSITIVITY: {他動詞|たどうし} (transitive). Pair: {折|お}れる (intransitive, to break/be folded). Pattern: Xを{折|お}る (break/fold X).

ASPECT: ている indicates completed action with result. {折|お}っている = 'has broken/folded.'

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{枝|えだ}を{折|お}る (break a branch)
・{骨|ほね}を{折|お}る (break a bone; also: to take pains)
・{紙|かみ}を{折|お}る (fold paper)
・{折|お}り{紙|がみ} (origami—noun)
・{心|こころ}が{折|お}れる (to lose heart—idiomatic, uses intransitive)

IDIOMS:
・{骨|ほね}を{折|お}る (to make great efforts, take pains)
・{足|あし}を{折|お}る (also: to interrupt, cut short)

HOMOPHONE: Don't confuse with おる (humble form of いる) which is different.
